home.intro: I was born in 2007 in Ankara. I taught myself economics from books, and this site collects the research and writing that came out of it.

work.title: Work
work.intro: A research paper and an essay, both written independently while preparing for university.

paper.metaLong: First draft December 2025, revised November 2026. 22 pages, in English.
paper.summary: Why do some people work informally by choice while others are pushed into it? The paper compares seven countries (Sweden, Germany, Italy, Estonia, Brazil, Argentina and Türkiye) and draws lessons for Türkiye.
paper.abstract: This paper examines the informal economy through an incentive-based institutional framework. It argues that informality arises from two distinct logics: voluntary avoidance driven by cost–benefit calculations and compulsory informality resulting from structural constraints. Drawing on Equity Theory and the Collective Action Problem, it identifies six institutional drivers of informality and compares seven countries: Sweden, Germany, Italy, Estonia, Brazil, Argentina and Türkiye. The comparison suggests that credible penalties discourage evasion, while recurring tax amnesties encourage it. Digitalization appears to be the most effective tool, because it prevents evasion without relying on the individual taxpayer’s initiative. For Türkiye, the paper argues that high inflation makes under-reporting easier, that heavy reliance on consumption taxes shifts the burden onto salaried workers, and that ending recurring amnesties and expanding digitalization offer a more durable path to formalization.

essay.metaLong: Written July 2026, revised November 2026. 4 pages, 18 numbered sources.
essay.title: Is It Possible to Leave the Healthcare System to the Private Sector?
essay.summary: Can healthcare be left to the market? A comparison of the United States, Taiwan and Türkiye, with numbered sources.
essay.long: Can healthcare be left entirely to the market? The essay looks at what happened to US charity hospitals when donations fell during the Great Depression, how Taiwan built a hybrid system after 1995, and how overuse and administrative costs strain the system in Türkiye.

about.title: About
about.p1: I was born in 2007 in Ankara, though my family is originally from Hekimhan, Malatya. I have a broad range of interests at the intersection of economics, software, data analysis and artificial intelligence. I focus in particular on software development with Python, data science and web technologies, and I keep improving my technical skills. I am currently preparing for the SAT, and I aim to continue my education in economics and data analytics in the United States.
about.p2: I designed this website as a digital portfolio that brings together my projects, my research and the results of my learning process. With the content I share here, I want both to document my own development and to offer a resource for people with similar interests.
about.p3: In the long run, I aim to combine technology and economics to produce projects with real added value, carry out academic research and contribute to the production of knowledge.
about.p4: Thank you for taking the time to visit my site.
